justice_ministers.name: Jody Wilson-Raybould
justice_ministers.notable: Tabled Bill C-14 (2016) — the original MAID legislation establishing 'reasonably foreseeable natural death' criterion. Resigned from cabinet in February 2019 over SNC-Lavalin affair.

justice_ministers.name: David Lametti
justice_ministers.notable: Tabled Bill C-7 (2021) REMOVING the 'reasonably foreseeable death' requirement after Truchon v Canada ruling. Bill C-7 created 'Track 2' MAID for people whose deaths were not reasonably foreseeable.

justice_ministers.name: Arif Virani
justice_ministers.notable: Oversaw Bill C-39 (2023) deferring mental-illness MAID expansion by one year, then Bill C-62 (2024) deferring again by three years to 2027.

health_ministers.name: Jane Philpott
health_ministers.notable: In office when C-14 passed. Physician by training. Resigned from cabinet with Wilson-Raybould (2019).

health_ministers.name: Ginette Petitpas Taylor
health_ministers.notable: Oversaw first Health Canada Interim Reports on MAID implementation — early data showing accelerating uptake.

health_ministers.name: Patty Hajdu
health_ministers.notable: COVID-era Health Minister during C-7 passage. Oversaw expansion to 'Track 2' non-terminally-ill applicants.

health_ministers.name: Jean-Yves Duclos
health_ministers.notable: Oversaw the 2022 Health Canada Fourth Annual MAID Report documenting 13,241 MAID deaths in 2022, 44% of the cumulative total to that date.

health_ministers.name: Mark Holland
health_ministers.notable: Tabled Bill C-62 (2024) deferring mental-illness MAID to 2027. Current-period Health Canada reports continue to document record-high MAID deaths.

senate_legal_affairs_committee_chairs.name: Bob Runciman
senate_legal_affairs_committee_chairs.notable: Chaired Senate LCJC during C-14 study and passage (2016). Committee accepted the 'reasonably foreseeable death' restriction that the Truchon ruling would later strike down.

senate_legal_affairs_committee_chairs.name: Mobina Jaffer
senate_legal_affairs_committee_chairs.notable: Chaired Senate LCJC during C-7 study. Committee amended C-7 to add mental-illness sunset clause — the expansion later deferred by C-39 and C-62.

truchon_ruling_principal.name: Jean-Pierre Truchon
truchon_ruling_principal.notable: His Quebec Superior Court challenge (Truchon v Procureur général du Canada) struck down the 'reasonably foreseeable death' criterion in 2019. The Trudeau government declined to appeal, accepting the ruling as the basis for Bill C-7.

expert_panel_on_maid_and_mental_illness.name: Dr. Mona Gupta (chair)
expert_panel_on_maid_and_mental_illness.notable: Chaired the federal Expert Panel on MAID and Mental Illness (2022 report). Panel recommended proceeding with mental-illness MAID expansion — a recommendation repeatedly deferred by Parliament since.

additional_oversight_actors.name: Catherine Ebbs
additional_oversight_actors.role: Canadian Human Rights Commission Chief Commissioner (during C-14 implementation)
additional_oversight_actors.notable: CHRC oversaw complaints during MAID's initial roll-out period. Disability-rights complaints filed.

additional_oversight_actors.name: Marie-Claude Landry
additional_oversight_actors.notable: Issued 2021 statement raising concerns about C-7 and disability rights — during the bill's final passage.

additional_oversight_actors.name: Chantal Petitclerc
additional_oversight_actors.notable: Paralympian senator who sponsored Bill C-7 through the Senate. Voted in favour of Track 2 expansion.

additional_oversight_actors.name: Yvonne Boyer
additional_oversight_actors.notable: Indigenous senator who raised concerns about MAID access disparities for Indigenous, rural, and disabled Canadians during C-7 and C-39 studies.

timeline.event: Supreme Court rules in Carter v Canada that the Criminal Code prohibition on assisted suicide is unconstitutional for competent adults with grievous and irremediable conditions.
Bill C-14 receives Royal Assent. MAID legal in Canada with 'reasonably foreseeable natural death' criterion.
First MAID Interim Report published — 2,704 deaths June 2016 through December 2016.
Quebec Superior Court in Truchon v Canada strikes down the 'reasonably foreseeable death' criterion.
Federal government tables Bill C-7 accepting Truchon ruling.
Bill C-7 receives Royal Assent. MAID expanded to Track 2 (death not reasonably foreseeable). Mental-illness sunset clause added by Senate amendment (original: 24 months).
CBC reports veteran Christine Gauthier was offered MAID by a Veterans Affairs caseworker. Similar cases from multiple veterans surface over following months.
Special Joint Committee on MAID tables report recommending mental-illness MAID expansion proceed as scheduled.
Bill C-39 receives Royal Assent. Mental-illness MAID expansion deferred to March 2024.
Fourth Health Canada Annual MAID Report: 13,241 MAID deaths in 2022 (4.1% of all Canadian deaths). Cumulative total exceeds 44,000.
timeline.source: Health Canada Fourth Annual Report on MAID

timeline.event: Bill C-62 receives Royal Assent. Mental-illness MAID expansion deferred again — to March 2027.
Fifth Health Canada Annual MAID Report: 15,343 MAID deaths in 2023 (4.7% of all Canadian deaths). Cumulative MAID deaths since 2016 now ~60,000+.
timeline.source: Health Canada Fifth Annual Report on MAID

timeline.event: Sixth Annual Report (prelim): ~17,000+ MAID deaths in 2024, continuing acceleration. Track 2 (non-terminally-ill) share growing.
timeline.source: Health Canada Sixth Annual Report on MAID

accountability_chain.constitutional_basis: Carter v Canada, 2015 SCC 5 — Supreme Court struck down absolute prohibition
statutory_framework: Criminal Code s. 241.2 (MAID provisions from C-14)
Criminal Code s. 241.2 as amended by C-7 — Track 2 added
accountability_chain.oversight_body: Health Canada — Annual Report on MAID
accountability_chain.oversight_body_limit: Reporting only; no compulsory power over provincial MAID practice or individual cases
accountability_chain.judicial_trigger: Truchon v Procureur général du Canada, 2019 QCCS 3792
accountability_chain.political_non_appeal: Trudeau government declined to appeal Truchon — chose legislative expansion (C-7) over defending the C-14 safeguard
accountability_chain.result_2024: ~60,000+ cumulative MAID deaths; 4.7% of all Canadian deaths in 2023; Track 2 non-terminal cohort growing; mental-illness expansion deferred to 2027 but politically contested
